source: GROUND.md §9.3. The effects library's catalogue, read by game/scripts/Fx/FxCatalog.cs. Sizes in metres (a billboard's full width; a streak's base length), speeds in m/s, lives and delays in seconds, cones in degrees; [a, b] is a range picked per particle; colours are linear [r, g, b]. Batches: spark, ember, flash, fire, dust, smoke, smoke_hero, haze, haze_rise, ring, droplet, chunk_stone, chunk_wood, chunk_metal (FxBatch.cs). dir: normal, up, down, along (the effect's direction), back, reflect, sphere, ring (outward along the surface). cap: how many may play at once; cull: metres from the camera past which it is skipped; hero: the moment the viewer's contact sheet shows; stage: what the viewer plays it on.

items.note: IW4 (GROUND.md §9.3): each item's effects by role, so a new gun, round or explosive is data, not code. A gun: muzzle (its shot's flash), muzzle:<attachment> (its shot with that part on its muzzle), backblast (out of its exhaust socket). An attachment: muzzle (its shot on any gun that takes it: the silencer's). A round drawn as its own model in flight: flight (a loop on it: a rocket's trail). An explosive, or a round with a blast: explode (where it goes off). What leaves a fire (explosives.json fires): fire (the loop it burns with, scaled to its radius over 3.5 m) and fireOut (the burnt patch it leaves). A deployable that burns fuel: fire (while it is lit).

effects.about: Rifle shot: a long flame, a flicker of light, a wisp of smoke, now and then a spark.
Rifle with a muzzle brake: the flame thrown out of the side ports, more smoke to the sides.
Pistol shot: a short, rounder flame, a smaller flicker.
Pistol with a muzzle brake.
Silenced: no flash and no light, only a small puff of smoke.
Rocket launched: a big flash at the muzzle, a burst of smoke ahead.
The launcher's back blast out of its venturi: flame, a cloud of smoke and dust behind the shooter.
A bullet's tracer: a short bright streak flying the bullet's path (some shots only).
An incendiary round's tracer: redder and a little brighter.
An arrow's faint trail: a thin pale streak behind it.

A rocket's motor burning (a loop on its tail, Direction its flight): a white-hot nozzle, a tongue of flame, sparks and a thick pale trail blasted back that hangs and spreads. Stop it when the motor burns out.
Bullet into earth: a burst of dirt, a puff of dust, clods, a scuff.
Bullet into grass: lighter dust, cut blades flung up, a few clods.
Bullet into sand: a fan of grains and a pale puff.
Bullet into rock: stone chips, grey dust, a spark or two, a chipped crater.
Bullet into wood: splinters, sawdust, a torn hole.
Bullet into metal: a spray of sparks off the plate, a flash, a wisp of smoke, a punched hole.
Bullet into water: a column of droplets, a white plume, rings spreading.
Bullet into a body: the blood hit (blood.hit).
An incendiary round's hit: orange sparks, a flare and a lick of flame (with fire.burning for what it sets alight).
A hit on a body: a short red mist and a few drops thrown along the shot, restrained.
A heavy hit (a head shot, a blast): more mist, more drops, still short.
Bleeding: a drop falling from the body and a small stain where it lands (play it on the ground under the bleeder).
A tool biting into a tree: wood chips and bark flying off, sawdust.
A hit on a tree's painted X: a bigger burst of chips and splinters, flecks of the red paint, a puff of sawdust.
A tool on stone: chips and grey dust.
A tool on ore: a shower of sparks with the chips.
A hit on the weak spot: a bright flash, a burst of glints and a ring off the surface.
An ore hotspot glinting now and then: a few tiny sparks and a twinkle.
A felled tree landing: a long low cloud of dust and litter along the trunk (Direction: the fall; Area: half its length).
An outcrop breaking: big chunks thrown out, a cloud of stone dust.
The timed charge: a white flash, a fireball, a dark column of smoke, dust thrown out along the ground, sparks, debris, a scorch mark, a hard shake.
The bag charge: dirtier and browner than the timed charge, less flash, more dust and clods.
The tin grenade: a sharp flash, a short fireball, tin shards and sparks, a smaller cloud.
A rocket's warhead: the biggest fireball, a heavy cloud, sparks, debris, scorch and shake.
An explosive round going off: a small pop of flame and smoke, sparks, a speck of scorch.
The incendiary rocket's burst (IRON_WAKE.md §7): a smaller blast, a flash, burning fuel thrown out in glowing globs that arc and fall, oily black smoke, a scorch; fire.patch burns on after it.
A charge that duds: the fuse sputters out in a few sparks and a puff of grey smoke.
A lit fuse (bag charge, tin grenade, timed charge): sputtering sparks and a thread of smoke (a loop on the item's fuse socket).
A lit campfire: tongues of flame, embers, a thin column of smoke, heat haze, a flickering warm light.
A lit furnace: flames in the firebox, a glow out of its door, smoke and the odd ember from the chimney.
A torch's flame (on its flame socket; FirstPerson for the one in hand): small tongues, embers, a wisp of smoke, a warm light.
Something burning (an incendiary hit, a burning player): a few licks of flame, embers, dark smoke.

An incendiary fire (IRON_WAKE.md §7; a loop, Duration 18, Scale its radius over 3.5 m): burning fuel over the patch, rolling flames, tongues of fire, embers, a column of oily black smoke, a flickering light.
An incendiary fire going out (where fire.patch burned, at its Scale): the last smoke, embers settling and the scorched, smouldering patch of burnt fuel it leaves.
A building piece coming down: a burst of dust over its area, debris, a light shake (Area: the piece's half size; Tint: the grade's colour).
A piece upgraded to wood: a puff of sawdust and shavings over it.
A piece upgraded to stone: grey dust and stone chips.
A piece upgraded to sheet metal: sparks and a puff of grey smoke.
A piece upgraded to armour: heavy sparks, dark smoke, a few hot fragments.
A door slammed shut: dust puffed out along its foot, motes shaken from its top (Area: half the door's width along Direction).
A step on sand: a kick of grains and a faint puff.
Something wooden breaking apart (gibs, GROUND.md §9.4): a puff of dust over it and splinters (Area: its half size; Tint: the material's dust colour).
Stone breaking apart (gibs): a heavy cloud of grit and chips (Area: its half size; Tint: the material's dust colour).
Metal breaking apart (gibs): a thin puff of rust and grime, torn bits of tin (Area: its half size; Tint: the material's dust colour).
A rock crumbling (gibs: an outcrop's last break): stone dust and gravel (Area: its half size; Tint: the material's dust colour).
Cloth and padding torn apart (gibs): a faint puff of lint (Area: its half size; Tint: the material's dust colour).
A fire place kicked apart (gibs): ash, a few embers and grit (Area: its half size; Tint: the material's dust colour).

A siege battery's shot (IRON_WAKE.md §6): a blinding flash, a fireball down the bore, a shock ring, a doughnut and a cone of gun smoke that linger, sparks, burning flecks, a hard light, a shake to 40 m.
The siege shot's blast on the deck or ground under the muzzle (Direction the barrel's along it, Tint the ground's dust): a low sheet of dust and grit swept out, more of it ahead, a pressure ring.
A defense mount's shot, one per barrel: a short, sharp flash, a jet of flame, the crack of a shock ring, a quick puff of smoke and sparks, so a ripple of three reads as three shots.

A battery rocket's motor lighting a few metres out (IRON_WAKE.md §6.4; on its tail, Direction its flight): a bright burst, a cough of flame, sparks and smoke back along its path; trail.rocket takes over.
A siege barrel's breech opening after the shot (normal out of it): a puff of spent propellant rolling out and a few hot specks; breech.smoke.wisps trails on while it stays open.
Smoke trailing from an open breech (a loop on its socket; Duration until the rammer closes it, about 2.2 s).
Ground wash under a lift engine (a loop on the ground below its nozzle; Tint the ground's dust): a low sheet of dust driven out, billows at its edge, grit, sand, bits of grass and leaves.
A boat's wake at its stern (a loop on the water's surface, by its speed; docs/MOTORBOAT.md): spray thrown up and back by the propeller, foam left on the water behind, rings spreading.
A bullet striking the Iron Wake's steel hull plate: a hard spray of sparks, a flash, a puff of paint and grit, a bright dent of bare steel in chipped paint.
A disabled battery or a hull below a quarter (a loop on it): heavy dark smoke pouring up, a smoulder of embers and a dim glow from the fire inside.
A ground vehicle's diesel at idle (a loop on each Exhaust_<n> point of its engine, VEHICLES.md §9.9; intensity: running): a thin blue-grey haze rising from the stack.
A ground vehicle's diesel under load (a loop on each Exhaust_<n> point; intensity: the engine's load): black soot pouring up and leaning back.
A diesel's black puff (at an Exhaust_<n> point; Scale: how hard): on starting, at a gear change and on a stab of the throttle.

Dust thrown up behind a tyre on the ground (a loop at its contact patch; Direction: behind it; Tint: the ground's dust; intensity: its speed and spin): a rolling cloud low behind it, grit and gravel kicked back.
Water thrown up by a tyre in shallow water (a loop at the water's surface by it; Direction: behind it; intensity: its speed): a rooster tail of drops and a mist over it.
